verdict.rationale: LangSmith documentation explicitly states you can 'Host an instance of LangSmith in your own infrastructure' for observability, evaluation, and prompt engineering, with Helm configuration guidance for self-hosted Agent Server deployments (langsmith-docs-17/23/32/39). However, community evidence suggests self-hosting is not the default lightweight/open path most users experience — one user explicitly wished for 'a locally hosted version that is easy to customize' and another built a workaround 'because LangSmith needs a cloud account to see my own traces,' implying self-hosting is not trivial or widely accessible in practice. Missing for 10: independent/hands-on confirmation that self-hosted deployment is easy or fully open (vs. enterprise-gated), and clarity on licensing/cost barriers to self-hosting.
